# Survey Sample International (SSI) 2012 Dataset
### Cultural Tastes, Social Demographics, and Aesthetic Perceptions of Americans
**Collected by Omar Lizardo & Sara Skiles**
:::

## Overview

Welcome to the repository and documentation website hosting the **Survey Sample International 2012 (SSI-2012)** dataset. This comprehensive dataset was collected by **Omar Lizardo** (UCLA, formerly University of Notre Dame) and **Sara Skiles** (University of Notre Dame) as part of a national sociological study investigating the cultural tastes, preferences, social stratification, and aesthetic perceptions of Americans.

This dataset provides a rich public resource for researchers, students, and practitioners interested in the sociology of culture, consumption practices, and social demographics.

---

## Sample and Sampling

The data come from an online survey fielded by Survey Sample International (SSI), a private firm that specializes in sampling and data collection. SSI drew respondents from its member database between February 28 and March 6, 2012. The sample was designed to approximate the U.S. adult population, with college graduates deliberately oversampled.

Quotas on age, gender, region of residence, education, and race/ethnicity governed admission. Once enough people with a given demographic profile had completed the survey, later applicants with that profile were screened out. Respondents gave informed consent, had to be at least 18, and received \$3.92 for completing the survey. SSI handled all payments.

Of the 3,782 people who opened the survey, 2,275 records remain after screening:

| Stage | Respondents |
|---|---|
| Opened the survey | 3,782 |
| Declined informed consent | 85 |
| Under 18 | 12 |
| Screened out because their demographic quota was full | 1,394 |
| Stopped within the first few screens (as reported; not flagged in the released data) | 16 |
| **Records in released data** | **2,275** |

The released data contain 2,275 records: 2,258 with a finished status of "complete record" and 17 with "some missing data." The dissertation reports 16 early stoppers as excluded, but the released data do not flag them. The partial records are included, consistent with the dissertation's condition and demographic counts. Filter on the `finished` variable to restrict analyses to completed surveys.

The survey software randomly assigned respondents to a control condition (529) or to experimental conditions (1,746). See the codebook for variable definitions.

### Known departures from the U.S. adult population

The sample does not match the U.S. adult population on every dimension. Skiles (2014) documents these departures:

- College graduates are overrepresented by design. About a quarter of respondents finished their education before taking any college courses, compared with 44% of U.S. adults.
- Adults aged 18 to 19 are slightly underrepresented (2.6% of the sample versus 3.9% of U.S. adults).
- Men aged 70 and older are overrepresented (8.4% of the sample versus 4.9% of U.S. adults).
- Because the survey was online, people without reliable internet access are probably underrepresented.
- The \$3.92 payment may not motivate high-income respondents, who are likely underrepresented.
- Other differences from the population, which the survey questions do not measure, are likely.

The source does not describe survey weights, and the codebook contains no weight variable. Users who need population-representative estimates should account for the design features above when interpreting results.

The authoritative description of the sampling procedures is Chapter 2 (Sections 2.1 and 2.3) of Skiles (2014), the dissertation that documents the survey behind this dataset. When describing sampling in your own work, cite it as:

> Skiles, S. (2014). *Aesthetic Taste Expression and Symbolic Boundary Work* (Version 1). University of Notre Dame. [https://doi.org/10.7274/z890rr19n23](https://doi.org/10.7274/z890rr19n23)
>
> The dissertation is also listed in ProQuest Dissertations & Theses (publication number 3731603): [ProQuest record](https://www.proquest.com/docview/1734428721)

## Dataset Scope & Key Topics

The SSI-2012 dataset covers a wide array of cultural, aesthetic, and demographic measures from a national sample of **2,275 Americans**:

### 1. Music Genres and Preferences
* **Genre Tastes**: 1–4 ordinal rating of liking/disliking for **20 distinct music genres** (ranging from Classical, Opera, and Jazz to Bluegrass, Hip-Hop, Indie, and Heavy Metal).
* **Listening History**: Binary check-all-that-apply indicators representing whether the respondent listened to each of the 20 genres in the past month.
* **Favorite Genre**: A single categorical measure identifying the respondent's favorite genre among all 20 options.

### 2. Cultural Stereotypes: Typical Fan Characteristics
* A large, multi-dimensional grid of **320 variables** (20 genres × 16 social characteristics) capturing the respondent's perceptions of the "typical fans" of each music genre. 
* Social dimensions include gender, race/ethnicity, education, age, and social class (e.g., whether a typical fan is female, college-educated, white, working-class, etc.).

### 3. Aesthetics & Painting Conformity Experiment
* The survey embedded an experimental design measuring aesthetic judgments. Respondents were shown an abstract painting and asked for their first impressions (`taste1`).
* They were then randomized into control and treatment groups and given social information about whether a reference group (varying in education and occupation) liked or disliked the painting (`alterlike`).
* They were asked how similar they felt to that group (`similarity`) and then asked to re-evaluate the painting (`taste2`). This allows researchers to model social conformity, taste mobility, and symbolic boundary-drawing.

### 4. Comprehensive Social Demographics
* Detailed respondent-level demographics including:
  * Gender, Age, and Census Region of Residence.
  * Race/Ethnicity (self-reported and individual indicators).
  * Education level (individual degree achievements and parents' college education status).
  * Current employment status and detailed occupational categories.
  * Pre-tax annual income and subjective social class self-identification.

## Dataset Cleanliness & Integrity

This distribution contains data that has been **comprehensively cleaned and properly labeled** for immediate scientific use:
- Categorical and ordinal variables carry embedded **Stata and SPSS value labels**. The R format keeps those labels, and the descriptive CSV writes them as text.
- Variables have been documented in a fully automated, interactive data dictionary.
